subject: Proposal: swap cohort stipend credits for a committed Dedicated discount
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Patel <ari@alphalab.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: swap cohort stipend credits for a committed Dedicated discount

Hi Ari,

Great talking earlier — following up with a concrete proposal so we can move quickly for the October cohort kickoff. AlphaLab provides each accepted startup with a $7k Redwood stipend. Several founders have expressed interest in converting that stipend into predictable, reserved Dedicated capacity (they want lower unit cost + guaranteed throughput for demo day).

Redwood is open to a one-time program exception: rather than issuing consumption credits, we can offer a cohort-level committed discount on Dedicated reservations in exchange for aggregating/escrowing the stipends. High-level outline attached (alphalab_pricing_table.csv):

- Option A (Aggregate swap): AlphaLab aggregates stipends for X startups (min 5) and converts the $7k per startup into a 6-month Dedicated commitment for pooled capacity. In return: 30% off standard Dedicated rate for the committed capacity.
- Option B (Hybrid escrow): Stipends are escrowed; Redwood provides a usage credit for Dedicated capacity up to N hours/month and any unused escrowed funds convert to a final invoice credit. This reduces risk for AlphaLab while keeping commitment flexibility.

Questions for you:
1) Would AlphaLab be able to aggregate at least five stipends per cohort?
2) Is AlphaLab open to a 6-month minimum commitment, or do you need a shorter window?
3) Any procurement/contract constraints around escrowing funds?

If this looks promising, we propose a short mutual action plan:
- Concord on option (A or B) and minimum cohort size by Sep 22
- Redwood drafts a term-sheet for the cohort by Sep 25 (attached: proposed-term-sheet.pdf)
- Finance/Legal sync and DocuSign by Oct 1 so commitments are in place before onboarding

I copied Marissa and Laura to help with pricing and finance constraints.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if helpful.

Best,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: alphalab_pricing_table.csv]
From: Ari Patel <ari@alphalab.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: AlphaLab Finance <finance@alphalab.io>
Date: 2025-09-18T17:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: swap cohort stipend credits for a committed Dedicated discount

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear options. A couple clarifying items before we share with the cohort leads:

- For Option A, does the 30% off apply to list Dedicated hourly rate or already-discounted reserved pricing?
- On minimum cohort size: we can aggregate 6 stipends reliably for Oct; would 6 be fine?
- Can you confirm how seat-level isolation works if startups want private environments later (i.e., can they opt out of the pooled commitment and keep a prorated balance)?

We have a short procurement freeze week starting Sep 24; would need anything DocuSign-ready before then to avoid delays. Finance is looped for the escrow question.

—Ari
Ari Patel
Program Manager, AlphaLab
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ari Patel <ari@alphalab.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-18T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: swap cohort stipend credits for a committed Dedicated discount

Ari — quick answers and a suggested conversion formula.

- The 30% is off our standard Dedicated reserved rate (it stacks on top of any PLG/promotional discounts but is applied to the standard per-GPU-hour list). We can make that explicit in the term-sheet.
- 6 startups is fine — that meets our minimum for a pooled commitment.
- Opt-outs: startups can opt out but the unused portion of a committed seat would be handled per the escrow/hybrid model; we recommend the escrow hybrid for cohorts where founders may self-select out after onboarding.

Conversion formula (suggested):
- Convert $7k stipend into equivalent GPU-hours using list Dedicated hourly rate R. For simplicity, we propose a 1.0x conversion (no additional markdown) and then apply the cohort 30% committed discount to the purchased block. Example attached in pricing CSV.

Laura — can you confirm finance's constraints on escrow vs. upfront committed invoices?

Thanks — happy to finalize option language.

Marissa
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-term-sheet.pdf]
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ari Patel <ari@alphalab.io>
Date: 2025-09-18T19:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: swap cohort stipend credits for a committed Dedicated discount

Marissa / Sean / Ari — finance here. High level constraints and one alternative to consider:

Constraints:
- We cannot book revenue or apply committed discounts against funds that are not contractually committed to Redwood. Escrowed stipends are acceptable only if AlphaLab (or the cohort vehicle) signs a short agreement authorizing Redwood to draw on escrowed funds for committed usage.
- Minimum monetary commitment per account grouping for discounting is $25k over six months. With 6 startups at $7k each = $42k, that clears the floor.
- Accounting prefers a single cohort-level PO or SOW that names AlphaLab as the contracting party; individual startups can still receive usage allocations but we need the legal counterparty to be AlphaLab or a named cohort vehicle.

Alternative (reduces procurement friction):
- Escrow + drawdown workflow: AlphaLab places stipends in escrow (custodial account) and signs a cohort SOW authorizing monthly drawdowns. Redwood invoices monthly for the drawdown amount and credits unused escrow back at the end of the term. This keeps procurement from requiring upfront prepay while giving Redwood contract certainty.

Next steps from finance side:
- If AlphaLab is comfortable with the escrow + SOW approach, we can draft the procurement language in 48 hours.
- If AlphaLab needs Redwood to accept an aggregated prepay from you (AlphaLab pays Redwood directly), we can issue a single invoice and treat it as prepaid committed revenue.

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: escrow-outline.xlsx]
From: Ari Patel <ari@alphalab.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: AlphaLab Finance <finance@alphalab.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-19T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: swap cohort stipend credits for a committed Dedicated discount

Thanks everyone — that all sounds workable. AlphaLab prefers the escrow + drawdown option to avoid a large upfront PO. We confirm we can aggregate 6 stipends for Oct.

Requesting next items:
- Redwood to share the draft cohort SOW + escrow authorization by Sep 20 so we can route through procurement during our freeze window next week.
- A DocuSign-ready SOW and a sample drawdown schedule (monthly) so finance can validate cashflow.

If you can get that to us by EOD Sep 20 we’ll aim to have signatures by Sep 26.

—Ari
Ari Patel
Program Manager, AlphaLab
